applies_why: This judge text uses Luke 2:48-49 and its two father-senses to label the issue UNDERDETERMINED, which is what K-S2 governs.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase "thy father" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to "my Father's business."
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: "A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand" — I weighed (1) treating the two father-references as simultaneous senses means the verse cannot be UNDERDETERMINED and both senses stand, against (2) the verse only fails to state the link or contrary, so UNDERDETERMINED is allowed under the first sentence.
why: The judge labels Luke 2:48-49 UNDERDETERMINED while acknowledging its two father-senses, so it treats as open what K-S2 says is not open and whose senses both stand.
